record.original_question: Starting with a single word, does the language of ﬁ- nite words constructed by iterating prefix-suffix square completion remains semi-linear?

evidence.quote: Starting with a single word, does the language of ﬁ- nite words constructed by iterating prefix-suffix square completion remains semi-linear?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma$. For a word $w \in \Sigma^*$, define the prefix-suffix square completion relation $\Rightarrow$ on $\Sigma^*$ as follows: $w \Rightarrow w'$ if either
(i) (suffix square completion) $w$ has a suffix of the form $yx y$ for some $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ with $y \neq \varepsilon$, and $w' = w x$ (so that $w'$ ends in the square $(yx)(yx)$ when read as $\dots y\,x\,y\,x$); or
(ii) (prefix square completion) $w$ has a prefix of the form $y x y$ for some $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ with $y \neq \varepsilon$, and $w' = x w$.

Let $\Rightarrow^*$ denote the reflexive-transitive closure of $\Rightarrow$. For a single word $w_0 \in \Sigma^*$, define
$$L(w_0) = \{ w \in \Sigma^* : w_0 \Rightarrow^* w \}.$$
Recall that a language $L \subseteq \Sigma^*$ is called semi-linear if its image under the Parikh map $\Psi : \Sigma^* \to \mathbb{N}^{|\Sigma|}$ (counting the number of occurrences of each letter) is a semi-linear subset of $\mathbb{N}^{|\Sigma|}$, i.e., a finite union of sets of the form $\{ v_0 + n_1 v_1 + \cdots + n_k v_k : n_i \in \mathbb{N}\}$ with $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k \in \mathbb{N}^{|\Sigma|}$.

Question: Is $L(w_0)$ semi-linear for every starting word $w_0 \in \Sigma^*$?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches concerning iterated prefix-suffix square completion turn up the original paper introducing the operation and follow-up work on the dual prefix-suffix square reduction (closure of regular languages, etc.), but no source explicitly resolves whether the language obtained by iterating prefix-suffix square completion from a single word is always semi-linear. The status therefore appears to be unknown/open based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Prefix-Suffix Square Completion
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces prefix-suffix square completion and studies properties of derived (infinite) words; does not resolve the semi-linearity question for the iterated language from a single word.
status_evidence.claim: Original work defines the operation but does not settle the semi-linearity problem.

status_evidence.title: Prefix–suffix square reduction - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the dual reduction operation and closure properties; the unbounded case for context-freeness/regularity is left open in places.
status_evidence.claim: Related follow-up work focuses on reduction rather than the semi-linearity of completion languages.
